name: Scrollytelling Data
description: Turns data into a scroll-driven HTML story.
author: AndrewHessMSFT
coverImageAlt: A long paper scroll turns scattered data dots into ordered bars, a trend ribbon, and a final orange insight marker.
coverImagePrompt:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: AI.Tedt.org skill gallery cover
Primary request: a long paper narrative scroll transforms raw data tokens into a sequence of clear visual story chapters
Scene/backdrop: uncluttered empty slate reading table with a warm paper scroll flowing through restrained architectural space and no decorative props
Subject: one continuous scroll passing through three chapter terraces where scattered dots become ordered bars, then a smooth trend ribbon, ending at one highlighted insight marker
Style/medium: premium editorial illustration with tactile dimensional detail
Composition/framing: exact 16:10 landscape; center the entire scroll, both rollers, all terraces, data forms, and insight marker within the inner 76%; leave the outer 12% on every side as quiet slate negative space
Lighting/mood: calm, capable, quietly technical
Color palette: warm paper #F8F6F0, slate #101820, navy #00446F, cyan #00A9E0, sparing orange #E86027
Constraints: no cropped scroll, roller, or data forms; no plants, vessels, spheres, or peripheral props; no text, letters, numbers, chart labels, logos, trademarks, or watermark; no paw imagery or paw logo; no cats or cat silhouettes; no product UI or Microsoft Fluent branding
